target_customer: Casual and enthusiast users wanting free browser-based layered image editing
problem: Photo editing needed expensive desktop software; a browser editor with layers brought Photoshop-style work to the web.
business_model: free web app, presumably ad supported

founders.name: Dave Brushinski
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Picnik
competitors.what: Flash based online photo editor with Flickr export
competitors.traction_then: Rated the best online editor by TechCrunch in Feb 2007

competitors.name: PXN8
competitors.what: Ajax photo editor with one-click enhance
competitors.traction_then: Previous top pick of TechCrunch before Picnik

competitors.name: Snipshot
competitors.what: Ajax editor formerly named Pixoh with a public API

competitors.name: Picture2Life
competitors.what: Ajax editor for images already online

technical_complexity.rationale: A Flash editor with layers, effects and image processing was hard for a one or two person team but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Layer support was the one differentiator and could be copied; TechCrunch questioned the target market for a tool too complex for casual users.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Adobe launched a web Photoshop beta in March 2008 and Flickr partnered with Picnik, which Google later bought, per the search results; no source shows an acquisition of Splashup.

market_need_then: Many web photo editors launched in early 2007 and TechCrunch ran a comparison, showing interest in browser editing as Flickr and photo sharing grew.

branding.domain_note: No website listed in the directory data; domain history not found.

identity.visual_style: Flash photo editor with a Photoshop-like interface

rebrands.why: Genbeta described it as a complete rebrand with improvements; no stated reason found.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch and blogs in 2007 and mentioned in later roundups, but no strong brand assets found.

outcome_analysis: Splashup, originally Fauxto, was a Flash layer-based photo editor praised by TechCrunch in early 2007 but its complexity left the target market unclear. Picnik became the favored editor through its Flickr tie, Adobe entered in 2008 and the company is inactive with only a tiny YC seed reported. No source states why it ended, so the cause is not public and the failure labels are inferences from the competitive timeline.
notes: The 10K seed with date 2007-06-25 rests on a single database (CB Insights); amount and investor unverified elsewhere. CB Insights lists Splashup as acquired but I found no acquisition and that page mixes in PicMonkey details, so exit is unknown; Crunchbase search snippet says closed. A search for a Corel acquisition found nothing. Competitor dates are from Feb 2007, before the S07 batch. Directory data has no website.
